schema: Bernard gloss overrides. Keyed by the exact lexicon key (lowercase printed form). Each value is an `edited` card the reader shows on click: { lemma?, pos?, gloss, note? }. Where `lemma`/`pos` are omitted the entry keeps Whitaker's. The note carries a treatise reference (chapter = Latin heading, e.g. 'Ch. II').

humilitas.gloss: humility — the way to truth; the virtue by which one is made low to oneself by truest self-knowledge.
humilitas.note: Bernard's definition, Ch. II: 'humilitas est virtus, qua homo verissima sui cognitione sibi ipse vilescit.' It is Christ's way ('Ego sum via'); its twelve degrees are the ladder to truth.

humilitatis.gloss: of humility; humility — the way to truth.
humilitatis.note: See 'humilitas'. 'duodecim gradus humilitatis' (Ch. III), the degrees to be ascended, per Benedict (Reg. 7).

humilitatem.gloss: humility (acc.) — the way to truth and the ladder's summit.

humilitate.gloss: by/through humility — the ascent to truth.
humilitate.note: See 'humilitas'. Bernard speaks of the fruit of humility, the reward of its ascent.

superbia.gloss: pride — love of one's own excellence; the descent opposed to humility.
superbia.note: Ch. IV: 'superbia … amor propriae excellentiae'. The proud man, like the Pharisaeus, exalts himself.

superbiae.gloss: of pride — the descending degrees Bernard traces.
superbiae.note: See 'superbia'. The work is titled 'de gradibus humilitatis et superbiae'.

superbiam.note: See 'superbia'. 'propter superbiam' Satan fell from truth (Ch. VIII).

charitas.gloss: charity — the sweet food that rewards the fully-ascended ladder; the gift of the Holy Spirit.
charitas.note: Ch. III: 'Vere dulcis et suavis cibus charitas'; per Benedict it crowns the twelve grades (Reg. 7). 'Charitas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum Sanctum' (Ch. VII). The extract spells it 'charitas'.

charitatis.gloss: of charity — the end of the humble ascent.
charitatis.note: See 'charitas'. 'in cellaria charitatis' — the fellow-brethren's hearts (Ch. VII).

charitatem.gloss: charity (acc.) — the reward of climbed humility.

curiositas.gloss: curiosity — the first degree of pride; the eye that wanders outward instead of guarding the heart.
curiositas.note: Ch. X: 'Primus itaque superbiae gradus est curiositas.' The curious monk feeds goats ('haedos'); the reprobate angel fell from truth through curiosity.

curiositatis.gloss: of curiosity — the first step of pride.

curiositatem.gloss: curiosity (acc.) — the first proud turning outward.
curiositatem.note: See 'curiositas'. 'per curiositatem a veritate cecidit' (Ch. X).

curiositate.note: See 'curiositas'. 'non simili quidem curiositate, sed mirabili charitate' (Ch. IX).

misericordia.gloss: mercy — compassion rooted in shared misery; Christ became merciful through the flesh.
misericordia.note: Ch. VI: Christ 'miser fieri ut misereri disceret'; 'Beati misericordes' (Mt 5:7).

misericordiam.gloss: mercy (acc.) — the pity learnt from suffering.

miser.gloss: wretched, miserable — one aware of his own wretchedness, the root of mercy.
miser.note: Ch. IV: 'vere miser es, et sic discas misereri'; Christ 'miser fieri ut misereri disceret' (Ch. VI).

miseria.gloss: misery, wretchedness — the shared condition out of which one learns compassion.
miseria.note: Ch. VI: 'de lacu miseriae et de luto faecis' (Ps 39:3); the brother's misery is felt by a 'misero corde'.

miseriam.gloss: misery (acc.) — the common wretchedness of humanity.

gradus.gloss: degree, step — one rung of the twelve-degree ladder of humility.
gradus.note: Benedict's 'duodecim gradus' (Reg. 7; Ch. I, III): degrees to be ascended, not counted, leading to truth.

gradibus.gloss: degrees, steps — the rungs of the ladder of humility.
gradibus.note: See 'gradus'. 'locuturus ergo de gradibus humilitatis' (Ch. I).

gradum.gloss: degree, step (acc.) — a rung of the ascent.
gradum.note: See 'gradus'. 'de gradu in gradum proficiunt' (Ch. II).

veritas.gloss: truth — the reward of humility; sought in oneself, in one's neighbour, and in its own nature.
veritas.note: Christ: 'Ego sum via, veritas, et vita' (Ch. I); 'cognitio veritatis fructus esse humilitatis'. Its three grades: in se, in proximis, in sua natura (Ch. V–VI).

veritatem.gloss: truth (acc.) — the fruit of humble ascent.

veritate.note: See 'veritas'. 'protinus in veritate …' Bernard urges the humble to stand in truth.

excessus.gloss: excess, rapture — a going out of oneself, toward God.
excessus.note: Ch. VI: the third grade of truth is reached 'per excessum contemplationis'; the prophet speaks 'in excessu suo: Omnis homo mendax' (Ch. V).

excessu.gloss: in excess/rapture — in a going out of oneself.
excessu.note: See 'excessus'. 'dixit in excessu suo: Omnis homo mendax' (Ch. V).

excessum.note: See 'excessus'. 'ad tertium per excessum contemplationis' (Ch. VI).

abraham.gloss: Abraham — the patriarch; from whose seed Christ took flesh.
abraham.note: Ch. IX: 'Verbum caro factum est … caro de carne Abrahae'; 'semen Abrahae apprehendit' (Hebr. 2:16).

pharisaeus.gloss: Pharisee — the proud man who thanks God he is not like other men.
pharisaeus.note: Ch. V: the proud Pharisaeus speaks 'in excessu suo: Deus, gratias ago tibi' (Lk 18:11), the contrary of the humble prophet's 'Omnis homo mendax'.

bernardi.gloss: Bernard of Clairvaux — the author ('of Bernard', gen.).
bernardi.note: Title and Ch. IX heading ('Gemitus et suspiria sancti Bernardi'): genitive of Bernardus.

godefride.gloss: Brother Godfrey — the Cistercian brother who asked Bernard to write this (vocative).

mundicordes.gloss: pure in heart — 'Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt' (Mt 5:8).
mundicordes.note: Pl. nom. of mundicors; Bernard: the third grade of truth is seen by a pure heart (Ch. II, VI).

elias.gloss: Elijah (Elias) — caught up ('raptus') into heaven (2 Kgs 2).
elias.note: Ch. VIII: 'Raptus est Paulus, raptus est Elias, translatus est Enoch' — unlike Christ, who was 'elevatus' by his own power.

heliu.gloss: Elihu (Heliu) — the speaker of Job 32, whose wine-like belly must vent.
heliu.note: Ch. XIII: the boaster bursts into 'Heliu verba': 'En venter meus quasi mustum absque spiraculo' (Job 32:19). NB: this is Elihu, not Elijah.

inculpabiliter.note: Ch. X: David and the Lord raise their eyes to ask and to give aid — 'ambo inculpabiliter'.

sion.gloss: Zion (Sion) — 'speculatio' (watchtower), the summit from which truth is seen.
sion.note: Ch. II: 'in culmine humilitatis … velut in Sion, id est in speculatione, … veritatem prospiciant.'

oblivisicitur.note: Ch. II: 'qui punire non oblivisicitur' — the source prints 'oblivisicitur' for 'obliviscitur'; a slip to correct in latin.md.

absalon.gloss: Absalom — David's son; 'spare the boy Absalom'.
absalon.note: Ch. IV: 'Parcite, inquit, puero Absalon' (2 Sam 18:5) — love's partial judgement, set against true judgement.

simon.gloss: Simon (Bar-Iona) — Simon Peter, blessed by the Father's revelation.
simon.note: Ch. VII: 'Beatus es, Simon Bar Iona, quia caro et sanguis non revelavit tibi, sed Pater meus' (Mt 16:17).

iona.gloss: Jonah (Iona) — 'Bar Iona' = son of Jonah; patronymic of Simon Peter.

enoch.note: Ch. VIII: 'Raptus est Paulus, raptus est Elias, translatus est Enoch'.

pedetentim.note: Ch. IX: 'ardua scala tutius pedetentim ascenditur' — the steep ladder is climbed step by step, more safely.

penultimo.note: Ch. XI: 'in penultimo levitas cohibetur' — levity is checked in the penultimate degree, mirroring the highest humility.

grossescere.gloss: to grow gross, swell (inchoative of grossus).
grossescere.note: Ch. XIII: once vanity grows and 'vesica grossescere coeperit' the boaster must vent or burst.

martha.gloss: Martha — sister of Lazarus (Jn 11); praised for her faith.
martha.note: Ch. XV: 'O Martha, magna nobis fidei tuae insignia tribuis'.
